solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Monkey about, turning up with mate mostly (8)

indicatorNotes.turning: turning a word over in a down-reading sense flips UP to PU
indicatorNotes.mostly: mostly takes all but the last letter

blocks.note: china = mate (rhyming slang: china plate), minus its last letter

annotation.surface: A monkey messing about, flipping upside down with its playmate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'China' for mate is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate. Monkey reads as a verb (to monkey about) but is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The capuchin is a small South American monkey.

entries.clue: Be annoyed with husband wasted in restaurant (4)

indicatorNotes.wasted: the husband is wasted, i.e. lost from the word

blocks.note: to chafe is to be irritated

annotation.surface: Someone fuming because their husband got drunk at a restaurant.
annotation.walkthrough: Wasted suggests drunk; here it just means thrown away, so the H goes.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a cafe is one kind of restaurant, the small informal sort.

entries.clue: Protected avian Progne with rail fence repositioned (9,6)

indicatorNotes.repositioned: the letters are moved to new positions

annotation.surface: A protected bird, Progne (a genus of martins), has its rail fence moved.
annotation.walkthrough: Progne is a genuine bird genus (the purple martins), which makes the surface plausible while its letters are just fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: The peregrine falcon is a bird of prey protected by law in Britain and elsewhere.

entries.clue: Nick succeeded with fresh way to get ball on the green (4,4)

annotation.definition: way to get ball on the green

blocks.note: a chip is a small nick
hot = fresh, as in hot news

annotation.surface: A golfer called Nick succeeds with a new technique for reaching the green.
annotation.walkthrough: Nick looks like a golfer's name; it is a small notch. 'With' just strings the parts together.
annotation.definitionFit: A chip shot is a short lofted stroke played onto the green in golf.

entries.clue: I assist over underpinning home (5)

indicatorNotes.underpinning: in a down clue, the reversed AID sits beneath IN

annotation.surface: Someone offering help to support the household.
annotation.walkthrough: The trap is reading 'I' as part of the wordplay; it is the whole definition, since India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: India is the word used for the letter I in the NATO phonetic alphabet.

entries.clue: Digital picture snapped minutes ahead of Associated Press (6)

blocks.note: snapped as in bit, like a dog

annotation.surface: A photo snapped minutes before it went out on the Associated Press wire.
annotation.walkthrough: Snapped suggests a photograph, fitting the picture; it actually means bit, as a dog snaps.
annotation.definitionFit: A bitmap is a digital image stored as a grid of pixels.

entries.clue: Prompt included just what’s needed before end of line (6)

indicatorNotes.end of: takes the last letter of line

blocks.note: 'it' is the very thing wanted, as in 'that's it!'

annotation.surface: A prompt or cue including exactly what is needed at the end of a line, like a theatre prompter.
annotation.walkthrough: Prompt reads as a noun, a theatrical cue; the answer is the verb, to prompt someone into action.
annotation.definitionFit: To incite someone is to prompt or urge them into action.

entries.clue: When women get gifts, sure thing to be exchanged in the next 24 hours? (9,6)

indicatorNotes.to be exchanged: letters that are exchanged trade places with one another, so SURE THING comes out in a new order
indicatorNotes.in: the rearranged letters go inside MONDAY

blocks.note: the day after Sunday, split MO…NDAY
anagram of SURE THING, placed inside

annotation.surface: A reminder that gifts for mothers are a sure thing to swap hands tomorrow.
annotation.walkthrough: The Saturday puzzle's 'next 24 hours' looks like Sunday itself, but the wordplay wants the day after the answer's Sunday, MONDAY. Mothering Sunday is the British Mother's Day, in Lent.
annotation.definitionFit: Mothering Sunday is the day in Britain when mothers receive cards and gifts.

entries.clue: Tot rum shop flogged here? (10)

indicatorNotes.flogged: beaten about, so the letters are knocked into a new order

annotation.surface: A naval port where tots of rum were sold, and sailors flogged.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: Portsmouth is the Royal Navy's home port, where the daily tot of rum and flogging both belong. Flogged also means sold.
annotation.definitionFit: Portsmouth, the historic naval base, fits a place of rum tots and floggings.

entries.clue: Socialise with European in trendy bit of country (8)

indicatorNotes.in: E goes inside the other letters

blocks.note: e = European, inserted after the T of INTRACT

annotation.surface: Mingling with a European in a fashionable rural district.
annotation.walkthrough: Bit of country reads like a slice of countryside, and a tract is exactly that; the E goes in after its first T.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: socialising is interacting with other people, a verb in both.

entries.clue: Vetoed president accepting Democrat after Foreign Office resistance (9)

indicatorNotes.accepting: a word accepting another takes it in, as a host accepts a guest, so BIDEN holds D
indicatorNotes.after: the president comes after FO and R

blocks.note: FO = Foreign Office, Britain's foreign ministry

annotation.surface: A president blocking something, taking a Democrat on board over Foreign Office objections.
annotation.walkthrough: Joe Biden is himself a Democrat, which makes the surface neat; resistance is the physics symbol, not opposition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what a veto blocks is forbidden, both past participles.

entries.clue: Provide food Charlie consumed with queen (5)

blocks.note: C is Charlie in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A caterer tells how Charlie ate alongside the queen.
annotation.walkthrough: Charlie looks like a person dining with royalty, but it is only a letter from the phonetic alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: catering is providing food, as caterers do at a wedding.

entries.clue: Leaves unstarted a long time (4)

indicatorNotes.unstarted: a word unstarted never gets its opening going, so the first letter is missing

blocks.note: the leaves of a book, with P dropped

annotation.surface: Someone who takes ages to get going when leaving.
annotation.walkthrough: Leaves reads as a verb (departs) or foliage; it is the pages of a book.
annotation.definitionFit: Ages means a long time, as in 'I waited ages'.

entries.clue: Competence shown by area division head (9)

annotation.surface: An area division head showing managerial skill.
annotation.walkthrough: Head looks like the boss of the division; it is a headland, as in place names like Sheerness.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: adeptness and competence both name skill at doing something.

entries.clue: Hysterical cry stopping United practising (10)

indicatorNotes.stopping: ROAR plugs a gap in PIOUS, as a stopper fills a hole

blocks.note: u = United, as in football club names
a roar is a cry, placed inside PIOUS after the P

annotation.surface: A hysterical shout interrupting a United training session.
annotation.walkthrough: Practising sounds like football training, matching United; it means religiously observant.
annotation.definitionFit: Uproarious means hysterically funny.

entries.clue: Old and proper affable, not Conservative (10)

indicatorNotes.not: 'not Conservative' means without the Conservative, so the C is taken out of CORDIAL

annotation.surface: An old-fashioned, proper, friendly person who is not a Tory.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old and proper' reads as a pair describing one person; only Old is the definition, and 'and' joins it to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Primordial means existing from the earliest times, very old.

entries.clue: What can finish up in pack split into cubes (5,3)

annotation.definition: What can finish up in pack

indicatorNotes.into: one thing split into another is put inside it, so RIFT is set into DICE

blocks.note: a rift is a split, placed inside DICE after the D

annotation.surface: Something that could end up in a rucksack cut into cubes.
annotation.walkthrough: Pack suggests luggage; it is pack ice, the dense floating sheet into which drifting ice can freeze.
annotation.definitionFit: Drift ice is floating ice that may end up packed together as pack ice.

entries.clue: Hand round sherry (4)

annotation.surface: Passing round glasses of sherry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hand round' looks like one instruction, to serve drinks; it splits into FIN and O.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by type: fino is a specific style of sherry, pale and dry.

entries.clue: Picked up very much lighter walker? (8)

indicatorNotes.Picked up: picked up by the ear, so we hear rather than see it

blocks.note: way = very much, as in 'way better'; fairer = lighter in colour

annotation.surface: Something picked up that is far lighter to carry on a hike.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a walker is only one kind of wayfarer, a traveller on foot.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a walker is one kind of traveller on the road, hence the question mark.

entries.clue: Royal servants ignoring the aged herald (4)

indicatorNotes.ignoring: ignoring something means passing it over, so YE is left out of YEOMEN

blocks.note: yeomen of the guard serve the monarch

annotation.surface: Royal servants passing over the elderly herald.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The aged' is not old people but 'the' in archaic form, ye, as in 'Ye Olde Tea Shoppe'. Herald is a noun here.
annotation.definitionFit: An omen heralds what is to come; it is a portent.

entries.clue: Desperate triad thugs reorganised (10)

indicatorNotes.reorganised: the letters are put in new order

annotation.surface: Desperate gangsters of a Chinese triad regrouping.
annotation.walkthrough: Triads are Chinese criminal gangs, so the thugs and their reorganising fit the surface perfectly.
annotation.definitionFit: Distraught means desperately upset.

entries.clue: Broach support on church (6)

annotation.surface: Raising the subject of propping up a church.
annotation.walkthrough: Broach suggests raising a topic; here it means to make a hole, as in broaching a cask.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in its physical sense: to broach a cask is to make a hole in it to draw off the liquid.

entries.clue: Having no illusions on the subject of boxer’s personal quirk (9)

blocks.note: a tic is a personal quirk

annotation.surface: A clear-eyed view about a boxer's odd habit.
annotation.walkthrough: Boxer almost always means Muhammad Ali in crosswords; the apostrophe simply drops out of the grid.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a realistic person sees things as they are, free of illusions.

entries.clue: Hollow boiler perhaps losing one energy (5)

indicatorNotes.losing: losing one means giving up the I, and the E fills the space it leaves
indicatorNotes.perhaps: a combi is one example of a boiler

blocks.note: a combi is a combination boiler
e = energy, takes the place of the I

annotation.surface: An empty boiler that has lost its energy.
annotation.walkthrough: Hollow reads as empty; it is a noun, a valley. A combe is a short valley, common in West Country place names.
annotation.definitionFit: A combe is a hollow or small valley in hillside.

entries.clue: Mock enemy soundly (4)

indicatorNotes.soundly: by sound, so heard rather than spelt

annotation.surface: Mocking an enemy thoroughly.
annotation.walkthrough: Soundly suggests thoroughly; it signals sound. Mock is an adjective, as in mock leather.
annotation.definitionFit: Faux means imitation or mock, as in faux fur.

entries.clue: More or less mean approach (4)

blocks.note: stingy, a third sense hidden between the other two
to come close to, as a verb

annotation.surface: An average approach, roughly speaking.
annotation.walkthrough: Three meanings in three words. More or less and mean look like maths; mean is stingy, as in 'near with his money'.
annotation.definitionFit: Three senses: near means approximately, near is old slang for stingy, and to near is to come close.

entries.clue: Cold comfort initially in what editor says for my chance (5)

indicatorNotes.initially: takes the first letter of comfort
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places the two Cs inside OUR, the way a thing sits in a box

blocks.note: the editorial 'we', so 'our' where others say 'my'

annotation.surface: An editor offering cold comfort about someone's slim prospects.
annotation.walkthrough: Editors use the plural 'we', so where you would write 'my' they write 'our'. Chance is a verb: to chance, to happen.
annotation.definitionFit: An old verb sense: to chance means to happen, and things that happen occur.

entries.clue: Varsity team arrived shortly before game (9)

indicatorNotes.shortly: cut short by its last letter

annotation.surface: A university side turning up just before the match.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Varsity' is British for the Oxford–Cambridge rivalry, as in the Varsity Match; Cambridge is one of the two teams.
annotation.definitionFit: Cambridge fields a team in every Varsity match against Oxford.

entries.clue: Maybe one slothful bowler lacking power (6)

indicatorNotes.lacking: a word lacking power is missing its P, which drops out of the bowler

blocks.note: a spinner is a slow bowler in cricket

annotation.surface: A lazy cricket bowler with no strength in his arm.
annotation.walkthrough: Sloth is one of the seven deadly sins, so a slothful person is one kind of sinner; 'maybe' marks the example.
annotation.definitionFit: Sloth is a deadly sin, so someone slothful is a sinner.

entries.clue: Shopper carrying item between two halves of beer (8)

indicatorNotes.carrying: BEER carrying the item holds it inside, as hands carry a tray between them
indicatorNotes.between: TRAY sits between BE and ER

blocks.note: BE and ER, the two halves

annotation.surface: A shopper at the bar carrying a tray between two half-pints.
annotation.walkthrough: To shop someone is British slang for informing on them, so a shopper is a betrayer, not a customer.
annotation.definitionFit: In British slang to shop someone is to betray them to the police.
